subject: genetics
question: **Type:** pedigree The pedigree below shows a family with an X linked dominant trait. An affected father has three daughters, all affected, and two sons, both unaffected. Which statement best explains this pattern? ```text PEDIGREE: Generation I: I-1 affected male x I-2 unaffected female Generation II: II-1 affected female, II-2 affected female, II-3 affected female, II-4 unaffected male, II-5 unaffected male Key inference: An affected father transmits the trait to all daughters and to no sons. Most consistent mode: X linked dominant ```

options.text: Daughters are affected because they inherit two X chromosomes, one from each parent
An affected father passes the mutant allele to all of his children, but only daughters express it
The sons are unaffected because X inactivation silences the mutant allele in males
An affected father passes his mutant X chromosome to every daughter and his Y chromosome to every son, so all daughters are affected and no sons are

explanation: An affected male has genotype *X^D Y* and passes his *X^D* chromosome to every daughter with probability 1 and his Y chromosome to every son, so all daughters are affected and all sons are unaffected. A describes the mechanics of X inheritance in daughters but does not explain why the trait appears, B is contradicted by the sons, who never receive the paternal X at all, and C confuses dosage compensation with transmission, because males do not inactivate their single X chromosome.
